title: kernel certification, pinning and controlled deprecation plan for attention and sparse-model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: As we onboard more model variants (dense MHA, grouped-QA/GQA, and sparse MoE), we need a repeatable process to certify kernel/compile variants, pin a model to a runtime profile, and safely deprecate older kernel artifacts. This ticket defines a certification matrix, automation for producing pinned profiles, validation criteria (perf + numeric), and a controlled deprecation/rollout plan that minimizes customer impact.

Problem: Currently model onboarding can land with experimental kernel variants that later regress or cause subtle numerical differences under quantization. There is no single mechanism to:
- produce a deterministic "certified" kernel profile for a model+arch+hardware tuple,
- atomically pin a model serving route to that profile and publish it, and
- deprecate older profiles with automated canary/rollback and audit trail.

Proposal:
1) Certification harness: an automated job that compiles all kernel variants for a model (fused MHA, grouped attention kernels, MoE routing kernels) across target hardware (A100, H100, L40). The harness will run a canonical validation suite: microperf (latency, p99), macroperf (tokens/sec, memory), and numeric regressions (logit-distance, deterministic seed runs).
2) Profile artifact: produce a single immutable profile file (profile-v{major}.{minor}+build) containing: kernel sha, compiler flags, kernel selection rules, hardware compatibility tags, tested seqlen/batch ranges, and a signature. Store in profiles registry and expose API for pinning.
3) Pinning API & UI: enable pin-by-default or pin-on-request for onboarding flows. Pinning ties a model-version to a profile artifact. Pin metadata must include owner, certification-run-id, and expiration windows for temporary pins.
4) Rollout & deprecation: staged rollout via canary on Dedicated pool -> Dedicated low-cost cluster -> Hosted for non-SLA customers. Deprecation marks profiles as deprecated in registry and schedules auto-migration tooling or manual remediation with notifications to customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Certification harness runnable for three representative models (one dense MHA model, one GQA-style grouped-attention model, one MoE model) across H100 and A100.
- Each run emits a signed profile artifact to the registry with semantic version and metadata.
- Pinning API implemented: POST /profiles/pin with audit log and TTL.
- Canary process defined: 1% traffic for 24h, spike test, automated rollback on p99 > baseline * 1.25 or token-error-rate increase > 0.1%.
- Numeric regression checks: logit L2 distance < 1e-3 on eval set and exact-token-match threshold >= 99% for deterministic prompts for pinned profiles.
- Console shows profile provenance, certification-run, and deprecation state.

Non-goals: full integration with console RBAC (follow-up ticket), long-term archival policies for binary kernels (>1 year).

Deliverables:
- certification harness (CI job + orchestration)
- profile registry contract and storage implementation
- pinning API and small console panel for profile details
- canary/rollback automation and runbooks
- migration tool to assist customer route rebindings

Testing & Validation Plan:
- Microbench: run microkernels with sequence lengths [16,64,512,2048], batch sizes [1,8,32], measure per-token latency and memory high-water.
- Macrobench: end-to-end inference on representative prompts measuring tokens/sec, end-to-end p50/p95/p99.
- Numeric: deterministic seeds, 50 canonical prompts, compute token-wise logit L2 and percent exact-match.
- Fault injection: mem pressure test to ensure graceful fallback to slower kernel when OOM risk detected.

Dependencies:
- ENG-15876 (kernel autotuner) for baseline autotuning knobs (not required but speeds tuning)
- Runtime infra work for signed artifact storage (S3 + signature service)
- Console team support for display and pin controls

Migration and rollback strategy:
- Certified profile is default for new model versions. For existing models, 30-day opt-in window after which an admin can schedule an auto-migration.
- Rollback triggers: perf/regression thresholds, customer error reports tagged with profile sha.

Longer-term follow-ups (future tickets):
- RBAC on pin/unpin, integration with release gating, and retrospective analytics on pinned-profile lifetimes and regressions.

acceptance_criteria: Three certified profile artifacts published and retrievable via registry API
Pinning API accepts POST and creates immutable binding with audit entry
Canary automation performs staged rollout and triggers rollback when thresholds exceeded
Console shows provenance, certification-run id, and deprecation state for profiles
Numeric regression checks pass for certified profiles on eval set
risks: Signed artifact storage lifecycle may increase infra costs if retention not limited
Edge-case numeric diffs under extreme quantization could still surface post-certification
Customer workflows that depend on implicit kernel behavior may need manual remediation during deprecation
